text.p: Belgian textile holding company Uniwear said on Monday it would issue up to one million new shares priced at 288 Belgian francs each.
"This capital increase shows the company's willingness to strengthen its position in the textile and leather industries," the company said in a statement.
The capital increase offer will run from March 3 to March 27 and is being arranged by Antwerp brokerage Smeets, Verbaet & Co, finance director Yves De Poorter told Reuters.
De Poorter said the price was the same as a separate capital increase last September, which was mainly subscribed by British linen spinning machine maker Mackie International Plc.
It was also the same as the strike price on 68,000 warrants issued by the company in 1995.

The company said it would hold a news conference on Friday, March 7, giving further details about the capital increase and its plans. The company said last September it would apply for a stock market listing in London.
De Poorter said 1996 results would be published around April 28.
